Notation as in the target. Write `e_U` for the indicator of a clopen set `U`.

**(4 ⇒ 1).** If `(X,T)` is conjugate to a subshift over the finite alphabet `A`, then `R` is generated by `u`, `u^(-1)`, the letter indicators `e_a` (`a ∈ A`) and the finitely many constants of `k`. Translates `u^(-t) e_a u^t` are coordinate indicators, and their products and sums give every locally constant function.

**(1 ⇒ 3).** This is `elementary-groups-over-fg-rings-have-property-t` (Ershov–Jaikin-Zapirain, Invent. Math. 179 (2010), Theorem 1.1).

**(3 ⇒ 2).** This is `discrete-kazhdan-groups-are-finitely-generated`: a discrete group with property (T) is finitely generated (Kazhdan; Bekka–de la Harpe–Valette, *Kazhdan's Property (T)*, Theorem 1.3.1, locator read at source by sk-verify-23).

**(2 ⇒ 1).** Let `S` be a finite generating set of `EL_n(R)`, and `R_0` the subring generated by the entries of the matrices in `S ∪ S^(-1)`. Every element of `EL_n(R)` is a product of such matrices, so all its entries lie in `R_0`. The matrix `e_12(r) = I + r E_12` lies in `EL_n(R)` and has `r` as an entry, so `R = R_0`.

**(1 ⇒ 4).** Let `r_1, …, r_m` generate `R`, and let `f_(ij)` be the coefficient functions of the `r_i`, so `r_i = Σ_j f_(ij) u^j`.

*The field is finite.* Each `f_(ij)` is locally constant on the compact space `X`, so it takes finitely many values. Let `k_0 ⊆ k` be the subring generated by all these values. The set of sums `Σ g_j u^j` in which every `g_j` takes values in `k_0` is a subring, because `(g u^i)(h u^j) = g·(h∘T^(-i)) u^(i+j)`. It contains every `r_i`, so it is all of `R`. It therefore contains the constants, so `k = k_0` is finitely generated as a ring.
A field that is finitely generated as a ring is finite, by the general Nullstellensatz for the Jacobson ring `Z`. For a finitely generated `Z`-algebra, the contraction of a maximal ideal is maximal and the residue field is a finite extension of the residue field of `Z`. Applied to the maximal ideal `0` of `k`, this gives `0 ∩ Z = pZ` for a prime `p`, and `k` is a finite extension of `F_p`.

*The system is a subshift.* Let `𝒫` be the finite clopen partition generated by the level sets of all `f_(ij)`. Let `ℬ` be the Boolean algebra generated by the sets `T^j P`, for `P ∈ 𝒫` and `j ∈ Z`. The set `R_ℬ` of sums `Σ g_j u^j` with every `g_j` `ℬ`-measurable is a subring, since `ℬ` is `T`-invariant. It contains the `r_i`, so `R_ℬ = R`, and every clopen subset of `X` lies in `ℬ`.
The itinerary map `x ↦ (the atom of 𝒫 containing T^j x)_(j ∈ Z)` is continuous and equivariant. It is injective, because clopen sets separate points and every clopen set is a finite Boolean combination of sets `T^j P`. So `(X,T)` is conjugate to a subshift over the finite alphabet `𝒫`.

**Model tests.**
- The note's subshifts over `F_2` satisfy item 4, and EJZ gives (T).
- The dyadic odometer over `F_q` fails item 4. Its ring is not finitely generated, which agrees with the reviewed `odometer-crossed-product-elementary-groups-not-kazhdan`.
- `k = Q` with any subshift fails item 4. The coefficient values of finitely many elements generate `Z[1/N]`, which does not contain `Q`.
